stories.headline: Virginia state Sen. Louise Lucas, one of the state’s most powerful Democrats, is charged with racketeering in a cannabis-business corruption case
stories.summary: Federal authorities on Thursday charged Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas, 82, with racketeering, a money-laundering conspiracy and conspiracy to distribute marijuana in an alleged public corruption scheme tied to a cannabis business she co-owns, NBC News reports. Lucas, a frequent Trump critic and one of the most powerful Democrats in Virginia, surrendered to authorities, and about half a dozen others, including her daughters, were also taken into custody. Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel flew to Norfolk to announce the charges, with Blanche saying Lucas put her own financial interests ahead of the people of Portsmouth and Chesapeake. NBC notes the investigation predates the Trump administration but that charging a political figure 12 days before a midterm election is unusual; Lucas is not on the ballot this year. In a statement she said she would not be intimidated, calling the case the full weight of the federal government "wielded against an 82-year-old great-grandmother."

stories.headline: iPhone Duo buyers are already lining up outside Apple Stores days before Friday’s launch, and the first preorders have shipped
stories.summary: With Apple’s first foldable iPhone going on sale Friday, buyers are already camping out at Apple Stores around the world, AppleInsider reports. Hundreds of people were lined up at Apple Galaxy in Macau a full 48 hours before launch, and a small walk-in line had formed at Apple Fifth Avenue in New York about 30 hours out, where staff were finishing giant iPhone Duo displays on the storefront. Apple has warned that retail stock will be limited on launch day, so many of those waiting may leave empty-handed. Meanwhile, preorder customers are starting to get shipping notices, with some orders already marked shipped for Friday, October 23 delivery. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 and sold out within minutes when preorders opened after Apple’s September 9 event.

stories.headline: Kyle Dubas says Ben Kindel collapsed 10 minutes into the Penguins’ flight but is home and could be back on the ice within days
stories.summary: Penguins GM Kyle Dubas gave a fuller account Thursday morning of 19-year-old center Ben Kindel’s medical scare on the team plane out of Salt Lake City, Pittsburgh Hockey Now reports. Dubas said Kindel collapsed about 10 minutes into the flight; team doctor Dr. Vyas gave him oxygen, he quickly regained consciousness, and he was taken by ambulance to the University of Utah Medical Center after the plane returned. Kindel has since been cleared and is back in Pittsburgh, and Dubas said he has no history of such an episode. The plan is more testing and medical clearance before a gradual return to training and practice, possibly with a short skate as soon as Sunday, though Dubas said the young forward was still “very clearly shaken.” Pittsburgh placed Kindel and Bryan Rust on injured reserve and recalled Rutger McGroarty and Chase Pietila ahead of tonight’s game against Florida.

stories.headline: LEGO and Daft Punk announce a full partnership, starting with a set of the duo’s “Alive 2007” pyramid stage
stories.summary: LEGO and Daft Punk officially announced a wide-ranging partnership on Thursday, and the first product confirmed is a set based on the French electronic duo’s famous “Alive 2007” tour pyramid stage, Consequence reports. The set began as a fan design by Patrick Harboun, known as RobotRock, and his young son, built during lockdown for a LEGO music contest and later backed by more than 10,000 supporters on LEGO Ideas before sitting in limbo for months. It turns out the holdup was a bigger deal: the collaboration will span products, content and brand experiences, with more announcements promised for 2027. The reveal, teased Wednesday on Daft Punk’s WDPK 83.7 broadcast, came with a short film set to “Voyager” and “Human After All” showing Daft Punk minifigures. No price, piece count or release date has been announced yet.

stories.headline: 1Password opens its vault to AI agents including Grok, letting them log in for you without ever seeing your passwords
stories.summary: 1Password has launched “1Password for Agents,” a system that lets AI assistants, including Grok, ChatGPT, Claude, Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots, use your stored logins to finish tasks like booking restaurants or buying gifts without the model ever seeing your username, password or vault, Engadget reports. When an agent hits a sign-in, it verifies itself to 1Password with a special key; 1Password then tells you which agent wants access and why, and if you approve, fills in the credentials and any one-time codes through its own secure channel. Access is granted per session, limited to specific approved items, and not carried over. Engadget cautions that while the agents can’t leak your passwords, they can still make mistakes like ordering the wrong item or booking a nonrefundable trip. Pricing and availability details haven’t been announced.

stories.headline: Macron says “illegitimate” protests will be banned after France’s worst riots in years, blaming “seditious” ultra-left groups
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said Thursday that “illegitimate” protests will be banned in the coming days, blaming “seditious” ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend’s riots and looting, NBC News reports. Speaking after a meeting with intelligence chiefs and senior ministers, Macron said union-organized marches could still go ahead but may be rerouted to protect businesses. Paris, Lyon, Lille and Grenoble had already banned demonstrations planned for Thursday, and Paris’s ban covers the Élysée Palace, both houses of parliament, main train stations and the downtown areas hit hardest by looting; night curfews are in place in parts of the capital. Authorities are bracing for a much bigger demonstration Saturday, when “yellow vest” activists are expected to join, and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu promised a “massive” security operation. Student groups say they will keep mobilizing despite the bans.

stories.headline: A Minnesota farmer found an 11-foot metal ring in his cornfield; it appears to be the upper stage of a Chinese rocket
stories.summary: A farmer in rural Stevens County, Minnesota, discovered a circular metal object about 11 feet wide in his cornfield, and it likely fell from space, Gizmodo reports. The piece matches the upper stage of a Zhuque-2E rocket built by Chinese company LandSpace, which launched September 15 from northwest China, delivered 10 satellites, and then made an uncontrolled reentry over the upper Midwest, where people reported fiery debris; the object had probably been sitting in the field for about six weeks. The sheriff’s office said it poses no danger. Half a world away, a car-sized, roughly 30-foot aluminum plate suspected to be from another Chinese rocket turned up on a palm oil plantation in Indonesia after residents heard a loud bang. Gizmodo says the cases add to concerns about China’s careless handling of falling rocket stages.

stories.headline: Ms. Rachel gives $3,000 to a GoFundMe for a Darien toddler whose library puppet-show video went viral
stories.summary: Children’s YouTube star Ms. Rachel has donated $3,000 to a GoFundMe for a 16-month-old boy whose visit to a Darien Library children’s event went viral, NBC Connecticut reports. A TikTok video showing the boy repeatedly trying to interact with a green puppet operated by a library employee, who appeared to ignore him and put the puppet away as the family left, has more than 6 million views. The family believes he was treated differently because of his skin color. Darien Library apologized, scheduled a call with the family, and said it is taking their concerns “incredibly seriously” and reviewing what happened. The fundraiser, started by the boy’s father, Micah Whitaker, aims to turn the experience into a happy memory with a family trip to Disney World; Ms. Rachel’s donation is its largest.

stories.headline: Satire: “Trump Aides Desperately Try To Explain Approval Rating Not Like Golf Score”
stories.summary: In this Babylon Bee satire, President Trump proudly boasts about a 36% approval rating, prompting aides to pull him aside with charts and explain that, unlike golf, a lower number is not better in politics. The fictional president insists it sounds like fake news, asks who hired the aide (he did), and decides a glass 36% full of Diet Coke still beats none. By the end of the piece, he has ordered staff to just scratch out the 36 and write in a better number, “like we do in golf.” This is satire, not a news report.

stories.headline: Hours after Witkoff’s talks with Putin, Russia fires three waves of ballistic missiles at Kyiv
stories.summary: Russia hit Kyiv with an intense overnight missile and drone barrage just hours after President Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg, ABC News reports. President Zelensky said Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles at the capital in three waves, striking homes, energy infrastructure, a railway station, the metro, shopping centers and even a monastery; at least two people were killed and 34 injured in and around Kyiv. Ukraine’s air force said none of the missiles were intercepted, while 181 of 210 drones were downed, and another Russian strike on a market in the Kharkiv region killed two more. Witkoff called his talks “constructive” and said trilateral technical-level talks will continue, but Zelensky called the strikes “demonstrative,” said they show “no real changes” in Moscow’s attitude, and jabbed at Witkoff’s description of Putin as a “humanitarian.” Ukraine answered with one of its largest drone attacks of the year on Moscow, which forced temporary closures at all four of the city’s international airports.

stories.headline: Judge refuses Lindsay Clancy’s lawyers’ bid to question the holdout juror who forced her mistrial
stories.summary: A Massachusetts judge has denied a request from Lindsay Clancy’s defense team to question the lone holdout juror who forced a mistrial in her triple-murder case, ABC News reports. Judge William Sullivan wrote that “any further judicial inquiry is inappropriate” because the court must not delve into a juror’s reasoning, views or relationships with other jurors, or into the jury’s deliberations. The jury split 11-1 in favor of finding Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity after a seven-week trial this summer. Her lawyers want the indictment dismissed, arguing the judge didn’t properly look into the holdout before declaring a mistrial, and had sought an evidentiary hearing on whether he lied on his questionnaire or used his phone during deliberations; Sullivan found they hadn’t shown they were entitled to one. Clancy, the former nurse charged in the 2023 deaths of her three children in Duxbury, is due back in court Nov. 2.

stories.headline: Apple reportedly boosts iPhone Duo orders by 44% to 14 million on the eve of Friday’s launch
stories.summary: Strong pre-orders have reportedly pushed Apple to order millions more iPhone Duo units from suppliers, MacRumors reports, citing DigiTimes. Supply-chain sources said Foxconn and component makers received instructions reflecting a roughly 44% increase, from 9.7 million to 14 million devices over a full 12-month period. Apple has called demand “nothing short of extraordinary,” and within 30 minutes of pre-orders opening Oct. 16, U.S. shipping estimates had slipped to Jan. 25 across every configuration. Hitting the higher target could still be hard: DigiTimes said output depends on assembly progress after earlier reports of trouble with assembly, displays and hinges. The $1,999 foldable launches Friday, Oct. 23.

stories.headline: Musk says his Terafab chip plant will make its first test chip by mid-2027, with real production in late 2028
stories.summary: Elon Musk said on Tesla’s earnings call that Terafab, the giant chip factory he announced in Austin in March, is “progressing quickly,” Gizmodo reports. “We’ll begin commissioning machinery in the first half of next year, and hopefully if things go well, we’ll make our first test chip, just to see if we can make any chip at all, around May or June,” he said, adding that “real production would be late ’28, which is lightning fast by fab standards.” Terafab is a joint venture between SpaceX and Tesla, which are also discussing a merger, and Musk said the two still have to work out who pays for what — “not going to be less than tens of billions in capital equipment through early 2028, and then it will probably be north of 100 billion long term.” Gizmodo notes chip fabs are notoriously slow and costly to build in the U.S., and that Musk has a history of optimistic timelines.

stories.headline: Jeep Wrangler production halted in Toledo after a nearby chemical leak forces evacuations
stories.summary: Stellantis halted production at the north plant of its Toledo Assembly Complex, which builds the Jeep Wrangler, after a hazardous chemical release about a mile away, CBT News reports. Workers were sent home Tuesday night and the first and second shifts were canceled Wednesday. The leak at the MC Tank Transport terminal on Progress Avenue involved glycidyl methacrylate, an industrial chemical used in plastics, paints and coatings that can irritate the eyes, nose, mouth and skin. Toledo Fire & Rescue ordered everyone within a mile to evacuate and those within three miles to shelter in place; by Wednesday evening the evacuation zone was cut to a half-mile and the shelter order lifted. City officials said tap water was not contaminated, and no serious injuries were reported.

stories.headline: Review: Tony Iommi keeps the Black Sabbath flame burning on his first solo album in 21 years, “From The Dark”
stories.summary: With Ozzy gone and Geezer Butler and Bill Ward all but retired, it falls to Tony Iommi to keep Black Sabbath’s fire going, and Louder’s review says he does on “From The Dark,” his first solo album in 21 years, out Friday. Teamed with Norwegian singer Jørn Lande, who co-wrote all eight songs and sometimes sounds uncannily like David Coverdale, Iommi works in the style of the Dio-fronted Sabbath and Heaven & Hell, backed by bassist Becky Baldwin and drummer Karl Brazil. Highlights include the hammer-to-the-anvil opener “Over The Violent Sun,” the “brutal boogie” of first single “World Alone,” “Stormwatcher,” and “Death Wake,” which features a lead break from Brian May. The reviewer saves the most praise for closer “Legacy,” calling it “absolute killer, gold-standard Iommi.”

stories.headline: Nikon’s Small World microscope-photo contest is won by a frozen-in-midair look at an inkjet printer laying ink on paper
stories.summary: Nikon has named the winners of its 52nd Small World Photomicrography Competition, which drew more than 1,800 entries from 69 countries, and first place went to an image of what happens inside a printer as it puts ink on paper, DPReview reports. German photographer Ole Bielfeldt, who creates under the name macrofying, built his own imaging rig around a microscope objective. His first tries failed because the printhead moved too fast to keep in focus and the droplets outran his shutter, so he reverse-engineered the printer to move the paper under a stationary printhead, then worked in a dark room and used a flash to freeze the droplets midair. “It turned out I already had everything I needed,” he said. The top 20 images also include views inside a pen and a pencil and plenty of cells.

stories.headline: Federal judge orders DHS to stop door-to-door noncitizen voter checks in nine states until Election Day
stories.summary: A federal judge ruled late Wednesday that the Department of Homeland Security’s practice of knocking on doors to ask people about their immigration status and recent voting likely violates the Voting Rights Act, CBS News reports. U.S. District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin ordered immigration authorities to stop “elections-related field operations and field interviews” in nine states, including California and New York, when they are likely to involve people officials know or should suspect are U.S. citizens. The order lasts until polls close on Election Day but is stayed until 5 p.m. Friday so the administration can appeal. The Trump administration says the operation is part of its crackdown on noncitizen voting. The judge wrote that investigating unlawful voting is not itself illegal but cited a “high likelihood of error” in how DHS built its target lists from agency and commercial data. The suit was brought by groups including the California Nurses Association and National Nurses United.

stories.headline: Garrett Wilson, targeted just twice before the fourth quarter in New England, says wanting the ball “ain’t disruptive” ahead of Dolphins week
stories.summary: Jets receiver Garrett Wilson is walking a fine line on his role in the offense, Heavy reports. After a 100-yard, touchdown game, he caught just four passes for 44 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Patriots and drew only two targets before the fourth quarter. Asked Wednesday by the AP how he can push for more targets without seeming like a malcontent, Wilson said, “it usually ain’t disruptive, like, let’s do it, you know, and that’s the mentality that all of us have being competitors,” adding, “For me, it’s kind of just getting my feet wet early and then, you know, let’s ride, I’m ready to go.” Heavy reads it as the team’s highest-paid player saying the right things while making clear he wants to be involved early. The Jets host the winless Dolphins on Sunday.

stories.headline: Trumbull’s Kids Pumpkin Fest is Sunday on the Town Hall Green with pumpkin decorating, a live DJ and touch-a-truck
stories.summary: Trumbull’s annual Kids Pumpkin Fest runs this Sunday, Oct. 25, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on the Town Hall Green at 5866 Main Street, Patch reports. The free family event features pumpkin decorating, face painting, lawn games, crafts and a live DJ, plus a touch-a-truck with the Long Hill Fire and Trumbull Police departments and crafts with the Trumbull Nature and Arts Center. Mobile coffee trailer Brewberry Cafe will serve a seasonal menu.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: a hearing on a one-year data center moratorium, early voting opens Monday at the library, and a Town Hall Halloween parade
stories.summary: Trumbull’s Planning and Zoning Commission will hold a public hearing Wednesday on a proposed text amendment that would define data centers as their own principal use in the town’s zoning rules and put a one-year moratorium on them, according to the meeting agenda, Patch reports in its weekly look at what’s coming up in town. Early voting for the Nov. 3 election runs Monday, Oct. 19, through Sunday, Nov. 1, at the Trumbull Library, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with longer 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29, according to the town clerk. Patch also points to First Selectman Vicki Tesoro’s statement on the proposed high-density housing development at 1, 7 and 15 Main St. in Monroe, near the Coventry Lane area of Trumbull; no application is pending in Trumbull, and residents can send comments to the Monroe Planning and Zoning Commission. The Commission on Aging will hear an update on fraud prevention and a Senior Center report, and preschoolers can trick-or-treat through Town Hall in the annual Halloween parade, which has two sessions of 20 children each and requires registration.
